sections.hypothesis: When Coinbase starts trading a coin that already trades on Binance, the coin's return against the other coins over the next 30 days differs from zero: up if new US retail demand keeps arriving (a lead for a long strategy), down if the listing marks a peak of attention (an exit rule for an altcoin portfolio). Either sign would be news; the study decides which, if either.
sections.rationale:
Who pays, if it rises: Coinbase is the main on-ramp for US retail; a listing widens the set of buyers, and demand that arrives slowly (as accounts notice and buy) would push the price up over weeks rather than at once. Who pays, if it falls: listings follow a run of attention and volume, and the same constrained-pessimism argument as the perp study (Miller 1977): the coin is priced by its most enthusiastic holders, and wider access brings sellers and arbitrage too.

Outside evidence (checked 2026-11-23): Li, Luo, Wang and Wei, 'Cryptocurrency Exchange Listings' (SSRN 4715718, 2025; AFT 2025) find positive short-term abnormal returns for listings on both Coinbase and Binance, larger on Coinbase (an average first-day return of 32.8% against 22.7%). A study of 390 cross-listings across 11 exchanges in 2020-21 (Laucht, Erasmus University thesis) finds abnormal returns positive before the listing and negative after the listing day. Messari's widely quoted +91% in five days (2021) was driven by a few outliers; Coin Metrics found 20-day results from -1% to +14%, with several coins falling. So the published effect is concentrated at and before the listing; the 30 days after, which this study measures (the part a Binance trader could act on after seeing the listing), is where reports disagree or find a reversal. Kestrel's own perp-listing study found coins lagged other coins by 15% in the month after their first perp listing (EXIT RULE, findings): a listing event can mark a top.

Why independent of the trend bet: the effect, if any, is each coin's own event against the other coins at the same time (abnormal return), not the market's direction. Expected overlap with the pursued strategies, stated before running: low in the abnormal return by construction; any strategy built on it would still hold coins, so its raw returns would carry crypto's market exposure, reported by kestrel overlap if it gets that far.

DISCLOSED: the listing-event family has one known result (the perp study, an exit rule), which shaped the expectation that a fall is at least as likely as a rise. Not a rejected family. Runs: one, a raw-effect study (not a trial).
sections.rules:
Universe: every stored Binance USDT pair that is a coin (kestrel.data.universe: no leveraged tokens, stablecoins, fiat, gold or tokenized stocks) outside the locked confirmation half: the exploration half plus the coins too young to have been split (kestrel.studies.events.open_universe). DISCLOSED: the first draft used the exploration half only; counting its events (dates only, no return read) gave 51 events on 40 listing days, under the 50 needed, so the universe was widened before any return was read. The confirmation half stays locked.

Events: each universe coin whose first trading day on Coinbase Exchange, the earliest daily candle across all its Coinbase products (USD, USDC, USDT, EUR, GBP, BTC...), came at least 60 days after its Binance spot history began (Binance first), with the 30-day window ending before 2025-11-01 (no holdout data). Dates from Coinbase's public API (kestrel ingest-coinbase-listings): only the first trading day is kept, no price is read. Counted on 2026-11-23 before any return was read: 519 universe coins, 174 traded on Coinbase by 2025-10-31; 72 events on 58 listing days (2019: 3, 2020: 6, 2021: 21, 2022: 18, 2023: 2, 2024: 5, 2025: 17). The rest were listed on Coinbase first, had under 60 days of Binance history, or ran into the holdout.

Day 0 is the UTC day of the first Coinbase candle. The announcement often comes days earlier, so the run-up window catches it. Returns from Binance daily bars, from day 1's open. Abnormal return over a window = the coin's return minus the equal-weighted mean return of every other universe coin that traded at both ends (as the perp study). Primary window: day 1's open to day 31's open. Reported, deciding nothing: day -30 to day 1 (the run-up), day 1 to day 8 (the first week), share of events below zero, by year. Same-day events are averaged into one; the bootstrap runs over listing days. Placebo: for each coin, 200 random days (seed 0) at least 60 days from its listing, the same window.

Run: kestrel event-study coinbase-listing (once).
sections.falsification:
Two-sided, so each side needs 95% rather than the perp study's 90%:
LEAD (worth a frozen strategy note, not a result) only if: at least 50 listing days; mean 30-day abnormal return at least +3%; bootstrap P(> 0) at least 95% (5,000 resamples, seed 0); above at least 95% of the placebo means.
EXIT RULE (a rule for an altcoin portfolio's note) only if: at least 50 listing days; mean at most -3%; P(< 0) at least 95%; below at least 95% of the placebo means.
INSUFFICIENT if fewer than 50 listing days. Otherwise KILL. Run once.
sections.parameters: Fixed before any return is read: 30-day primary window from day 1's open; at least 60 days of Binance spot history before day 0; equal-weighted market adjustment; 200 placebo days a coin at least 60 days from its listing; 5,000 resamples, seed 0; thresholds +-3% and 95%. No other window, universe or filter is tried; a change is a new version with a reason.
sections.costs: A measurement, not a strategy run: returns before costs. The +-3% bar is set against the cost of acting on it (a round trip in a small coin, two taker fees of 7.5 bps and its half-spread band twice, about 0.5%). Not a trial (a raw-effect study); recorded in the findings.
